questions.question: Front wheel brakes work:
questions.explanation: Front wheel brakes work in all road conditions. Even on ice, front wheels rarely skid.

questions.question: A truck's weight affects:

options.text: Less than the type of cargo.

questions.explanation: A truck's weight is a major factor in stopping distance. Heavier trucks need more braking power to stop.

questions.question: When approaching a bridge or overpass, you should:

options.text: Not trust the posted clearance height.
Measure the height before going under it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not trust the posted clearance height.
questions.explanation: Do not assume posted heights are accurate. Road repaving or snow can change the actual height. If you are unsure your vehicle fits, slow down and find another route.

questions.question: Aggressive driving means:

options.text: Driving selfishly or in a pushy way.
Driving safely with respect for others.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving selfishly or in a pushy way.
questions.explanation: Aggressive driving is selfish, pushy driving that ignores the safety and rights of other drivers.

questions.question: In heavy traffic, the safest speed is:
questions.explanation: Match the speed of surrounding traffic. Vehicles traveling at the same speed cannot hit each other.

questions.question: Before a trip, inspect your windshield. Do NOT:

options.text: Remove and sharpen the wiper blades.
Check the wipers for proper spring tension.
Check the wiper blades for damage.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove and sharpen the wiper blades.
questions.explanation: Check your windshield for cracks. Check wiper arms for proper spring tension and wiper blades for damage or stiff rubber. Do not remove or sharpen blades.

questions.question: Road rage is:

options.text: Driving with intent to harm others.
Driving a vehicle that has not been inspected.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving with intent to harm others.
questions.explanation: Road rage means driving with the intent to harm others or physically assault another driver or their vehicle. This is different from aggressive driving.

questions.question: On a steep downhill road, you should:

options.text: Use a low gear and engine braking.
Downshift instead of using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a low gear and engine braking.
questions.explanation: On long or steep downhills, use engine braking mainly to control speed. Use brakes only as extra help.

questions.question: The top cause of death and injury in work zones is:
questions.explanation: Speeding causes most deaths and injuries in work zones. Drive carefully around workers.

questions.question: If you must drive onto the shoulder in an emergency, you should:

options.text: Get both wheel sets onto the shoulder.
Stay on the shoulder until you stop, if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay on the shoulder until you stop, if possible.
questions.explanation: Stay on the shoulder until your vehicle stops. Then signal, check mirrors, and merge back safely. Avoid hard braking on the shoulder above 20 mph. Keep one wheel set on the pavement if you can.

questions.question: In an S-cam brake, friction is created when the brake shoes and linings:

options.text: Press against the outside of the brake drum.
Press against the inside of the brake drum.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: Friction is created inside the brake drum when brake shoes and linings press against the inside of the drum. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.

questions.question: What type of force do emergency brakes use?
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three parts: the service brake, the parking brake, and the emergency brake. The emergency and parking brakes use mechanical force.

questions.question: When traveling slower than 40 mph, keep at least ____ of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: At speeds below 40 mph, allow at least one second of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle. At faster speeds, use the same formula and add one more second. Larger vehicles need more space to stop than smaller ones.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop if your brakes fail while driving downhill?

options.text: Let the vehicle slow down on its own.
Let rumble strips slow your vehicle.

questions.explanation: If your brakes fail on a downhill slope, quickly find an escape ramp to stop your vehicle. If no escape ramp is available, drive into an open field or side road that is flat or goes uphill.

questions.question: What is a tire load?

options.text: The minimum safe weight a tire can carry
The maximum safe weight a tire can carry

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe weight a tire can carry
questions.explanation: Tire load is the maximum safe weight that a tire can carry at a certain pressure.

questions.question: A cardboard box on the roadway:

options.text: Should be expected to be on the roadway.
Could contain a heavy object that could damage vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Could contain a heavy object that could damage vehicles.
questions.explanation: Any object on the road is dangerous. A cardboard box may look harmless but could contain something heavy or hard that damages your vehicle.

questions.question: If there is a fire in your vehicle, you should not:

options.text: Park in an area away from buildings, trees, brush, and other vehicles.
Notify emergency services of your problem and your location.

questions.explanation: If your vehicle catches fire, leave the road and stop in an open area. Do not pull into a service station because the fuel there could catch fire. Call emergency services and tell them your location.

questions.question: Before trying to put out an engine fire:

options.text: The engine should be turned off.
The accelerator should be pressed to use up fuel.

questions.correctAnswerText: The engine should be turned off.
questions.explanation: If your engine catches fire, turn off the engine as soon as you safely can. Do not open the hood when trying to put out the fire.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will be asked to:

options.text: Explain what you would inspect and why.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain what you would inspect and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must do a complete inspection of your vehicle. Tell the examiner what you are checking and why you are checking it.

questions.question: When alley docking, you should first:

options.text: Position your vehicle directly in front of the alley.
Back up directly in front of the alley.
Stop parallel to the outer boundary of the alley.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop parallel to the outer boundary of the alley.
questions.explanation: To alley dock, pass the alley first and stop your vehicle parallel to the outer edge. Then back your vehicle straight into the parking space between the boundary lines.

questions.question: While driving, a driver should:

options.text: Not worry about what is happening on the sides of their vehicle.
Pay attention to what is happening on all sides of the vehicle.
Not worry about what is happening behind the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pay attention to what is happening on all sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: You must be aware of what is happening on all sides of your vehicle at all times. Look ahead and check both side mirrors regularly while driving.

questions.question: Roads are especially slippery when it first begins to rain because:

options.text: The fresh rain mixes with oil on the road.
The water has nowhere to go.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fresh rain mixes with oil on the road.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, it mixes with oil that has dripped onto the road. This creates a slippery, dangerous surface.

questions.question: Wheels with welding repairs are:

options.text: Safe to use if a professional did the repairs.
Safe to use if the repair looks solid.

questions.explanation: Wheels or rims with welding repairs are not safe. Replace them before driving the vehicle.

questions.question: An Individual Vehicle Distance Record (IVDR) does not need to include which of the following?
questions.explanation: An IVDR must include the distance traveled and fuel purchased. It must have the trip dates and total distance. It does not need to include how many vehicles were passed.

questions.question: When traveling on a downgrade, your vehicle will:

options.text: Travel at the same speed as on level roadway.

questions.explanation: Gravity causes your vehicle to speed up when going downhill. Slow down before you reach a downgrade.

questions.question: Convex mirrors:

options.text: Cannot be used on vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
Help drivers see a larger area.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help drivers see a larger area.
questions.explanation: Many large vehicles have curved convex mirrors. They allow drivers to see a wider area than flat mirrors. However, objects appear smaller and farther away than they actually are.

questions.question: When exiting a vehicle, a driver should:

options.text: Jump directly from the seat to the ground.
Keep at least one point of contact with the vehicle.

questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle, face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. For a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly may cause you to fail the basic vehicle control skills test.

questions.question: Too much air pressure in a tire:
questions.explanation: Tires should never have too much air pressure. Always check your tire air pressure with a gauge during inspections.

questions.question: When applying your brakes, the vehicle should:
questions.explanation: If your vehicle pulls to one side when braking, it may indicate a brake problem.

questions.question: To use the controlled braking method, you should:

options.text: Press the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
questions.explanation: Controlled braking means applying the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels. Keep steering wheel movements very small when using this method.

questions.question: What is traction?

options.text: Grip between the tires and the road
How long it takes for the brakes to start working

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip between the tires and the road
questions.explanation: Traction is the grip between your tires and the road surface. Good traction is needed to brake and steer safely.

questions.question: Which of the following is acceptable during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Front tire tread of 3/32 inch deep

questions.explanation: Check that front tires have at least 4/32 inch of tread depth. Other tires need at least 2/32 inch of tread depth. All tires on a vehicle must be the same size.

questions.question: Which is a required emergency equipment item?
questions.explanation: All commercial vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes spare electrical fuses, three reflective warning triangles or six fuses or three flares, and at least one working fire extinguisher.

questions.question: If one-fourth of the leaves in a leaf spring are missing during inspection:

options.text: The driver can continue driving at lower speeds.
The vehicle must stop being used until it is repaired.
The vehicle is safe to drive because most of the spring is still there.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle must stop being used until it is repaired.
questions.explanation: Check the suspension for broken or missing leaves in leaf springs. This is a serious defect. If one-fourth or more of the leaves are missing from any leaf spring, the vehicle must be taken out of service.

questions.question: When transporting cargo, drivers must check the cargo tie-downs every:
questions.explanation: Check cargo tie-downs within the first 50 miles of a trip. Then check them again every three hours or every 150 miles.

questions.question: If another vehicle is tailgating you in a large vehicle, do all of the following except:

options.text: Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead

questions.explanation: If tailgated, increase your distance from the vehicle ahead and avoid sudden moves. Speeding up will only cause the other driver to tailgate at a higher speed. Do not flash your brake lights.

questions.question: What is brake lag?

options.text: The delay between pressing the brake pedal and the brakes starting to work
The space between the brake pedal and the floor
The amount of air pressure used to stop the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: The delay between pressing the brake pedal and the brakes starting to work
questions.explanation: Air takes time to travel through the brake lines to the brakes. Air brakes do not work instantly. There is usually at least one-half second of delay between pressing the brake pedal and the brakes beginning to work.

questions.question: The ____ between an air compressor and reservoir tank stops air from leaking if the compressor fails.
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve must be installed between the air compressor and the main reservoir. It stops air from leaking out of the system if the air compressor develops a leak.

questions.question: When transporting cargo, you should inspect the load:

options.text: Only after traveling a long distance

questions.explanation: Inspect the cargo and tie-downs before starting your trip. During the trip, check them within the first 50 miles, every three hours or every 150 miles, and after every break.

questions.question: When loading cargo, place the weight:
questions.explanation: A vehicle can tip over if its center of gravity is too high. Distribute cargo weight evenly and keep it as low as possible.

questions.question: What do air storage tanks do?

options.text: They are not allowed on a vehicle.
They store compressed air for the brakes.
They should be drained of excess air after every trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: They store compressed air for the brakes.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold the compressed air that powers the brakes in an air brake system. Different vehicles have different numbers and sizes of tanks.

questions.question: What should you do before driving your vehicle?

options.text: The inspection report is not important.
The inspection report only matters if passengers will be in the vehicle.
Review the previous inspection report if one exists.

questions.correctAnswerText: Review the previous inspection report if one exists.
questions.explanation: Start your vehicle inspection by reading the last inspection report. Only sign the new report if any problems from before have been fixed.

questions.question: How should you check a belt-driven air compressor belt?
questions.explanation: Check the air compressor belt before each drive. The belt should be tight and in good condition.

questions.question: What makes up the emergency brake system?

options.text: Only parts of the parking brake system
Only parts of the service brake system
Parts of both the parking and service brake systems

questions.correctAnswerText: Parts of both the parking and service brake systems
questions.explanation: An air brake system has three separate braking systems: service brakes, parking brakes, and emergency brakes. The emergency brake system uses parts from both the parking and service brake systems.

questions.question: What does rust around wheel nuts mean?
questions.explanation: Check your tires before every drive. Rust around wheel nuts is a sign that they may be loose.

questions.question: What happens if you drive a commercial vehicle with any alcohol in your system, even if below the legal limit?

options.text: You will be taken out of service for two hours.
You will be taken out of service for 10 hours.
You will be taken out of service for 24 hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will be taken out of service for 24 hours.
questions.explanation: If any alcohol is found in your system while driving a commercial vehicle, even if your blood alcohol level is below 0.04 percent, you will be taken out of service for 24 hours. Driving under the influence is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: At 55 mph on dry pavement, how many feet does brake lag add to your stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance includes four parts: how far you see ahead, how far you travel while reacting, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your total stopping distance.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage allowed for a triple combination vehicle during a one-minute static leakage test?
questions.explanation: During a static leakage test, a triple combination vehicle with air brakes should not lose more than 5 psi in one minute. If it loses more than this, something needs to be repaired before you drive.

questions.question: When should you start a left turn?

options.text: Before reaching the center of the intersection.
At or after the center of the intersection.
After your rear wheels have passed the center of the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or after the center of the intersection.
questions.explanation: Wait until you reach the center of the intersection before turning left. If you turn earlier, the left side of your vehicle could hit other drivers because large vehicles do not turn in a tight circle.

questions.question: When driving a 50-foot truck at 50 mph, how far back should you stay from the vehicle ahead?
questions.explanation: Below 40 mph, allow one second of distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle length. At higher speeds, use the same formula and add one more second.
